0.0.n: This is the name of a Japanese discount-store chain.

0.1.n: Marks Daiso as the source of the product.

0.2.n: Past form of 出る, describing a product that has come out.

0.3.n: Combines 新, meaning new, with 商品, meaning product.

0.5.n: Combines with ネット to name a mesh bag used when washing clothes.

0.6.n: A borrowed English word; here it refers to a mesh laundry bag.

0.7.n: A borrowed English word naming the item that holds the laundry nets.

0.8.n: Politely ends the sentence identifying the product.

1.0.n: Names the task that tends to cause difficulty.

1.1.n: Marks what causes difficulty in the pattern 〜に困る.

1.2.n: 困る becomes 困りがち to express a tendency toward difficulty; な connects this description to 洗濯ネット.

1.3.n: Forms 洗濯ネット with the next word, naming a mesh bag for washing clothes.

1.4.n: Japanese does not mark singular or plural here; the context refers to laundry bags generally.

1.5.n: Marks the laundry nets as what you hook onto the holder and store.

1.7.n: Indicates the nets can be hung directly, without further preparation.

1.8.n: Politely points to the holder being shown.

1.9.n: Links こちら to ホルダー to mean this holder.

1.10.n: Refers to the product introduced in the previous line.

1.11.n: Marks the holder as the place where the nets are hooked.

1.12.n: The て-form of 引っ掛ける connects hooking the nets with storing them.

1.13.n: Pairs with できます to say that putting the nets away is possible.

1.14.n: Polite form of できる; after 収納, it expresses that the nets can be stored.

2.0.n: Refers to the rear of the holder.

2.1.n: Marks where the magnet is attached.

2.2.n: Makes the back surface the topic, following に to keep the location meaning.

2.3.n: Names the part attached to the holder's back.

2.4.n: Marks the magnet as the thing that is attached.

2.5.n: 付く + ている describes an attached state; the final て links it to the next part.

2.7.n: Combines with 横 to specify the side of the appliance.

2.8.n: Follows 洗濯機 directly, without の, to name a possible mounting location.

2.9.n: Shows that the washing machine's side is one example, not the only option.

2.10.n: Refers generally to magnets when describing suitable surfaces.

2.11.n: Marks magnets as what sticks to the surface.

2.12.n: Plain form of 付く, written in hiragana; 磁石がつく describes the surface that follows.

2.13.n: Describes the shape of a suitable mounting surface.

2.14.n: Connects 平ら to 面 so it describes the surface.

2.15.n: Is described both as flat and as something magnets stick to.

2.16.n: Marks the surface where the holder can be mounted.

2.17.n: Polite ability form of 取り付ける, expressing that you can mount the holder.

0.lit: A new product released from Daiso: a laundry net holder it is.
0.tip: 出た comes before 新商品 to describe it: a product that came out.

1.lit: Laundry nets often troublesome for storage, as they are, onto this holder hooking, you can store.
1.tip: 引っ掛けて links the action of hooking the nets to storing them, showing how they are stored.

2.lit: On the back, a magnet is attached; to flat surfaces magnets stick to, like washing-machine sides, it can be mounted.
2.tip: 磁石がつく describes 面: a surface that magnets stick to.
